hook: A polarity-switching phthalimide lets four-electron Li-I2 pouch cells run past 1000 cycles.
summary: A phthalimide molecule changes from electron-poor to electron-rich as the battery charges, first trapping iodine species to stop them shuttling, then stabilizing the reactive I+ state. Flexible Li-I2 pouch cells reached about 400 mAh per gram of iodine and over 1200 Wh per kg of iodine. Cathode-level energy is lower, at about 883 Wh per kg, and results are for lab-scale cells.
title: Switchable nucleophile-electrophile chemistry enables functional four-electron Li-I2 batteries
